solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Excellent bishop that’s retired put to work since (7)

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the pair reads backwards

blocks.note: ace means excellent
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to use something is to put it to work

annotation.surface: A first-rate bishop who has stepped down is being made to work again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests the bishop's career, but it applies to ACE B together, turning them round.
annotation.definitionFit: Since and because both introduce a reason: 'since you asked' means 'because you asked'.

entries.clue: Live Wagnerian opera’s characteristic cold sound (6,6)

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
Wagner's Ring cycle, often just called the Ring
the S of the possessive is used as it stands
a trait is a characteristic

annotation.surface: A live performance of Wagner has a distinctively chilly tone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' pretends to be noise, following 'opera'; here it is a sea channel, and the Bering Strait between Alaska and Siberia is very cold.
annotation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of sea, and the Bering Strait is a famously icy one.

entries.clue: Show taxi ranks combined over the radio? (7)

indicators.note: a radio carries only sound, so the words are heard not seen

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi and an array is a set of ranks; run together they sound like the show

annotation.surface: A radio presenter talks up a line of taxis waiting in ranks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ranks' looks like a taxi rank, the place cabs wait; here it means rows, an array.
annotation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a show of songs and sketches in a club or restaurant.

entries.clue: Doctor beginning to puncture delusion, as nice as it was (9)

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of PUNCTURE
the other eight letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A doctor sets out to burst a patient's delusion that things are as good as ever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' sits at the head of the clue like a physician; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Something unspoiled is still as nice as it was originally.

entries.clue: Make the sound of an eagle (4)

indicators.note: we want a word that sounds like the bird, not the bird itself

blocks.note: the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle

annotation.surface: Someone is asked to imitate an eagle's cry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make the sound of an eagle' reads as one instruction to screech; 'Make' alone is the definition, as in making money.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the money sense: what you make in wages you earn.

entries.clue: Find Charlie back before Henry has left (4,2)

indicators.note: Henry's H goes away from the phrase

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
HOME BY means back before a set time; H for Henry is dropped

annotation.surface: Someone must locate Charlie and bring him back before Henry goes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back before' is one phrase, HOME BY, as in 'be home by ten'; H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance, so 'Henry' is an H.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: you come by a rare book when you happen to find and acquire one.

entries.clue: Clubs the right place for goalscorers, left-winger thought (10)

blocks.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
a football attacker must be onside to score
a red is a left-winger in politics

annotation.surface: A football pundit muses on where a club's strikers and wingers should stand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left-winger' and 'Clubs' paint a football team; the winger is a political one, a socialist red.
annotation.definitionFit: Considered, as a past tense, means thought over.

entries.clue: Look pleased putting second last number on the clock (5)

indicators.note: SMILE's S is moved to a new position
the S goes to the end of the word

blocks.note: SMILE, with its S taken off to move
S is the abbreviation for second, and is SMILE's first letter

annotation.surface: Someone smiles happily as they set a clock to its last second.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The clock' is not a timepiece but a car's mileometer, which counts the miles driven.
annotation.definitionFit: The number shown on a car's clock, its odometer, is the miles it has done.

entries.clue: This put a stop to wound leaking in the morning? (7)

indicators.note: the AM seeps out of DAMAGE

blocks.note: to ban something is to put a stop to it
DAMAGE, a wound, loses AM, the morning

annotation.surface: A dressing that stops a cut bleeding overnight, applied in the morning.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a bandage, but 'This' alone is the definition; AM is the usual shorthand for morning.
annotation.definitionFit: 'This' points to the answer itself: a bandage is the thing that stops a wound leaking.

entries.clue: Try to get shiny gem with discount? (3)

indicators.note: a discount takes something off, here the last letter

blocks.note: RUBY with its Y knocked off

annotation.surface: Someone hopes to buy a sparkling jewel at a reduced price.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shiny gem' reads as one phrase; 'shiny' belongs to the definition, and the gem is simply a ruby.
annotation.definitionFit: Rubbing something is an attempt to polish it until it shines.

entries.clue: Small quantity of ink left in well (10)

indicators.note: INK and L are placed inside SPRING

blocks.note: a spring is a well; its first part
used as it stands
L is the abbreviation for left
the rest of SPRING closes round them

annotation.surface: Only a little ink remains at the bottom of an inkwell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small quantity of ink' reads as one phrase; 'of' is the link, and 'ink' is wordplay, not the thing measured.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun from the verb: a few drops or grains scattered over something, a light scattering.

entries.clue: Composer associated with Hallelujah once, Handel or other? (7,5)

indicators.note: the letters are made into something other

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: The man behind Hallelujah: was it Handel once, or someone else?
annotation.walkthrough: Handel's Hallelujah Chorus makes him look like the answer; the other Hallelujah is Leonard Cohen's song.
annotation.definitionFit: Leonard Cohen wrote and first recorded the song Hallelujah in 1984.

entries.clue: Fine pointer that’s showing north west (6)

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left, so N goes first

blocks.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
an arrow is a pointer

annotation.surface: A slender compass needle points north-west.
annotation.walkthrough: 'North west' looks like a compass bearing; 'west' only says where the N sits.
annotation.definitionFit: Fine and narrow both mean slim, as in a fine or narrow margin.

entries.clue: Fail to find gallery, say in error (8)

blocks.note: to miss something is to fail to find it
the Tate is a London art gallery

annotation.surface: A tourist can't locate the art gallery and blames a wrong direction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' tempts as 'for example'; it is part of the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The prefix MIS- means wrongly and state means say, so the word is built from its definition.

entries.clue: Walk to church, perhaps large building full of ghastly silver (10)

indicators.note: PILE is filled with GRIM and AG

blocks.note: a pile is a large building; its first part
grim means ghastly
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the E of PILE closes round them

annotation.surface: Worshippers walk to a vast church crammed with gaudy silverware.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large' looks like L, which would be natural, but the whole of 'large building' is PILE.
annotation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place; 'perhaps' because not every pilgrimage ends at a church.

entries.clue: Spying device in place across area revealing behaviour (9)

indicators.note: SITE stretches across A and TELL

blocks.note: a site is a place; its first letter
A is the abbreviation for area
in poker a tell is behaviour that gives your hand away
the rest of SITE

annotation.surface: A bug planted somewhere in the neighbourhood exposes what people get up to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In place' looks like one phrase meaning installed; 'in' is only the link.
annotation.definitionFit: Spy satellites orbit the earth photographing what happens below.

entries.clue: Beautifully cut patch with a hole in it? (5)

annotation.definition: Beautifully cut patch with a hole in it?

blocks.note: the surface wants a tailored patch of fabric; the setter means a stretch of immaculately mown grass
the surface wants a torn garment; the setter means a golf hole, the cup the ball drops into

annotation.surface: A tailor's finely trimmed patch that has a hole in it anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut patch with a hole' suggests sewing; the patch is a golf green, closely mown, with the hole in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A putting green is a smooth patch of short grass with the hole in it.

entries.clue: Contrive to lose snap? (3,4,2)

blocks.note: British slang for managing to be rid of something unwanted
read literally, to get a shot of something is to snap it with a camera

annotation.surface: Someone tries to lose their temper, or a photograph.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: 'get shot of' taken word for word is taking a photo.
annotation.definitionFit: Get shot of is British slang for get rid of; get a shot of is to photograph.

entries.clue: Nifty pseudonym such as Dr Dre? (5)

blocks.note: Dr Dre is a rapper, so his name is a rap one
a stage name is an identity, ID

annotation.surface: A clever stage name, like the one Dr Dre uses.
annotation.walkthrough: Dr Dre is the American rapper Andre Young; his stage name is a rap ID.
annotation.definitionFit: Nifty can mean quick and agile, as rapid does.

entries.clue: Recipe that expressly includes particular intolerance (3,4)

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the words before it

blocks.note: reciPE THAT Expressly

annotation.surface: A recipe spells out that it caters for a food intolerance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intolerance' suggests a food allergy, matching 'recipe'; here it is dislike.
annotation.definitionFit: A pet hate is the particular thing a person cannot stand.

entries.clue: Publican’s offering class A drugs to Spooner (5,4)

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: A-class is the best; it takes the G sound from its partner
gear is slang for drugs; it takes the B sound in exchange

annotation.surface: A pub landlord is found to be selling heroin and cocaine.
annotation.walkthrough: Class A is the UK's most serious drug category, but read here as 'best'; a guest beer is a changing extra ale a pub stocks.
annotation.definitionFit: A guest beer is a beer a pub offers for a limited time alongside its regulars.

entries.clue: Easy compact net’s middle and sides given alternating pattern (7)

indicators.note: the middle of a word, like the middle of a row, is its central letter
the sides of NET are its outer letters, N and T
the two pieces take turns, E then NT, over and over

blocks.note: middle letter of NET
outer letters of NET
the middle again, alternating
the sides again
the pattern ends as it began

annotation.surface: A tidy folding net whose centre and edges are woven in a chequered design.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Easy compact' sounds like something handy to pack; a compact is an agreement, and an entente is an easy, informal one.
annotation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between states, less formal than a treaty.

entries.clue: Confused at lingo on one engraved stone (8)

indicators.note: confused means jumbled together, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: seven letters to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Someone is baffled by the jargon about an inscribed stone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like the link to the definition, but the I it joins goes into the mix too.
annotation.definitionFit: An intaglio is a gem or stone with a design cut into its surface.

entries.clue: One wears medal about to be sold at auction (5)

annotation.definition: about to be sold at auction

indicators.note: the medal is worn, so it sits round the I

blocks.note: a gong is slang for a medal; its first part
I is the Roman numeral one
the rest of GONG

annotation.surface: A veteran's medal is about to go under the hammer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One wears' reads the wrong way round: I is inside GONG, as a wearer is inside clothing.
annotation.definitionFit: The auctioneer calls 'going, going, gone' as the lot is about to be sold.

entries.clue: Picture frames likely to burn, touching light (6)

indicators.note: PIC goes round HOT like a picture frame

blocks.note: PIC is short for picture; its first letter
something hot is likely to burn you
the rest of PIC

annotation.surface: Framed photographs may get scorched if hung in direct light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Touching' means 'concerning', so the definition is 'to do with light'.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical adjective from Greek phos, light; 'touching' is used in its sense of 'concerning'.

entries.clue: Attack retreating force showing little fight (4)

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so FIT reads backwards

blocks.note: a fit is an attack, as of coughing
F is the symbol for force in physics

annotation.surface: An army falling back after an attack shows little appetite for battle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attack' reads as military, next to 'force'; it is a fit, a sudden bout.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with 'little' doing real work: a tiff is a petty, short-lived squabble, not a brawl.

entries.clue: Celebrity on principle is most demanding type (10)

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing 'on' another is placed after it, as if added on

blocks.note: a maxim is a principle
A-list celebrities are the most famous

annotation.surface: A star who refuses to compromise on principle is the pickiest sort of client.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Celebrity on principle' sounds like someone famous on principle; the A-list is the top tier of celebrities, so a celebrity can be the A-list itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A maximalist demands the most, refusing to settle for less.

entries.clue: A lack of finale for sluggish drama (3)

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: no means a lack of, as in no time
last letter of SLUGGISH

annotation.surface: A slow play falls flat for want of a proper ending.
annotation.walkthrough: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama, famously stately in pace, so 'sluggish drama' is a fair joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Noh is a form of traditional Japanese theatre.

entries.clue: Thin male bore (6)

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave that surges up a river

annotation.surface: A skinny man who is tedious company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as a dull person; it is the tidal wave on a river, also called an eagre.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of scanty: a thin or meagre helping.

entries.clue: Side with props providing little support in drained fountain (7)

indicators.note: to be in something is to be enclosed by it, so IF and TEE sit between F and N
a drained fountain has its insides emptied, leaving F and N

blocks.note: first letter of FOUNTAIN
providing means if
a golf tee is a small support for the ball
last letter of FOUNTAIN

annotation.surface: Stage props hold up a small part of a dried-out fountain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Props' look like stage furniture; they are rugby forwards, and a rugby union side is a fifteen.
annotation.definitionFit: A rugby union team is a fifteen, and props play in its front row.
